text: Gerard Kuiper discovered Nereid, a moon of Neptune, on photographic plates taken with the 82-inch telescope at McDonald Observatory.
Astronomers using the TRAPPIST telescope at ESO's La Silla Observatory announced three planets orbiting the ultracool dwarf star TRAPPIST-1, about 40 light-years away.

source.title: ESO: Three Potentially Habitable Worlds Found Around Nearby Ultracool Dwarf Star (eso1615)

text: Charles Messier logged the globular cluster M3 in Canes Venatici, his first original discovery for his catalogue.
NASA's Magellan probe was launched from Space Shuttle Atlantis, the first deep space probe launched by a shuttle. It went on to map about 98 percent of the surface of Venus.
Gottfried Kirch and Maria Margarethe Kirch first saw the globular cluster now known as M5 while they were observing a comet.
Barnaba Oriani discovered the spiral galaxy M61 in Virgo. Charles Messier saw it the same night but mistook it for a comet.
Willem de Sitter was born in Sneek, the Netherlands. He built models of the universe from general relativity and proposed that it expands.
Mercury passed across the face of the Sun. Transits in May are rarer than those in November because they happen about a month after Mercury's aphelion.

source.title: NASA Eclipse Web Site: Catalog of Transits of Mercury

text: Charles Messier cataloged the globular cluster M4 in Scorpius and was the first to resolve it into a cluster of faint stars.
Mercury crossed the face of the Sun in a transit lasting more than seven hours, and NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory recorded it in near real time.

source.title: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio: Mercury Transit Live Shots May 9, 2016

text: James Dunlop discovered the galaxy NGC 1808 and described it as a faint nebula.
Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin was born in Wendover, England. She went on to show that stars are made mostly of hydrogen and helium.
Pierre Méchain discovered the Sombrero Galaxy, now known as M104, in Virgo.

Space Shuttle Atlantis launched on the fifth and final servicing mission to the Hubble Space Telescope, which installed Wide Field Camera 3 and a new ultraviolet spectrograph and repaired two instruments.
Astronomers of the Event Horizon Telescope collaboration unveiled the first image of Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way.

source.title: ESO: Astronomers reveal first image of the black hole at the heart of our galaxy

text: James Dunlop discovered the globular cluster NGC 6388 using a 20 cm reflector.
John Tebbutt of Windsor, New South Wales, discovered the Great Comet of 1861 about a month before it reached perihelion.
ESA's Herschel Space Observatory and the Planck spacecraft lifted off together on an Ariane 5 rocket from the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana.
The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument began its five-year main survey on the Nicholas U. Mayall Telescope at Kitt Peak.
Williamina Fleming was born in Dundee, Scotland. At Harvard she classified stellar spectra and found 10 novae, 52 nebulae and hundreds of variable stars.

source.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Williamina Paton Stevens Fleming

text: Nancy Grace Roman was born in Nashville, Tennessee. Known as the Mother of Hubble, she spent years championing the space telescope and winning its funding.

source.title: Astronomy: May 16, 1925, The birth of Nancy Grace Roman

text: Norman Lockyer was born in Rugby, England. With Pierre Janssen he is credited with discovering the gas helium.
Arthur Schuster photographed the sungrazing Comet Tewfik during a total solar eclipse, the first photograph of a comet taken during an eclipse.

source.title: Astronomy: May 17, 1882, Comet Tewfik is spotted during an eclipse

text: The Hubble Space Telescope took the second of the discovery images of Nix, a small moon of Pluto found by Max Mutchler and Andrew Steffl of the Pluto Companion Search Team.
Koichi Itagaki first observed the supernova SN 2023ixf in the Pinwheel Galaxy, M101.
The Hubble Space Telescope took its first image with the Wide Field/Planetary Camera, a view of stars around HD96755 in the open cluster NGC 3532 in Carina.

source.title: Space.com: Hubble Telescope Opened Its Eyes 25 Years Ago Today

text: Williamina Fleming died. At Harvard she discovered 10 novae, more than 50 nebulae including the Horsehead Nebula, and the first known white dwarf.

source.title: Astronomy: May 21, 1911, The death of Williamina Fleming

text: Thomas Gold was born in Vienna. He helped develop the steady-state theory of the universe.
Charles Messier independently found the globular cluster M5 in Serpens and described it as a round nebula without stars.
Nicolaus Copernicus died in Frauenburg, East Prussia, in the year his book proposing that the planets circle the Sun was published.
William Herschel discovered the elliptical galaxy NGC 5982 in Draco.
The first unit telescope of ESO's Very Large Telescope at Paranal saw first light and returned scientifically useful images on the night of 25 to 26 May.

source.title: ESO: First light for the VLT (eso9820)

text: The SOFIA airborne observatory saw first light and returned images of the core of the galaxy M82 and of heat escaping from Jupiter.

source.title: Wikipedia: Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy

text: Astronomers at Yerkes, Harvard, Allegheny and Urbana observatories used photoelectric cells to turn light from the star Arcturus into current that lit the central building of the Chicago World's Fair.

source.title: University of Chicago Library: Yerkes Observatory at the Century of Progress 1933 World's Fair

text: James Dunlop discovered the spiral galaxy NGC 1566, later known as the Spanish Dancer.
Frank Drake was born in Chicago. He devised the Drake equation and led Project Ozma, the first systematic search for radio signals from other civilizations.
Charles Messier discovered the globular cluster M10 in Ophiuchus and entered it as number 10 in his list.
Expeditions to Principe and Sobral in Brazil observed a total solar eclipse to test Einstein's prediction that the Sun's gravity bends starlight.
Charles Messier discovered the globular cluster M12 in Ophiuchus and described it as a nebula without stars.
Martin Schwarzschild was born in Potsdam. He studied stellar structure and red giants and led the Stratoscope balloon telescope projects.
